A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDOT-PNCG research, with matching authors, methods and principal experiments. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original solver benchmarks, parameter ablations and scaling experiments on MNIST, color transfer, synthetic OT problems and DOTmark.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and additionally reports exact-solver and IPOT comparisons in Figure 5, Table 1 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The proposed solver retains geometric temperature annealing, entropy-aware stopping and smoothing, extrapolated warm starts, rounding, and the same PNCG preconditioner and line search. Rewritten pseudocode and KL-projection terminology do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: MNIST, color transfer, synthetic entropy-controlled problems and all ten DOTmark datasets already appear in v3. The new comparisons use retained tasks; problem sizes up to n = 16384 were also already evaluated.

E2.justification: v4 adds the CPU network-simplex solver as a timing comparator in Figure 5 and Table 1, and directly evaluates IPOT in Figure 9. v3 explicitly omitted IPOT comparisons because of its similarity to MSK. Existing comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include relative-error and speedup comparisons at n = 4096 and 16384 in Table 1. Appendix G uses explicit matrix reductions, gamma_i = 2 and gamma_f = 2^15, then continues MDOT projections at fixed final temperature to match IPOT's operation budget. These are additional settings, not demonstrated revisions to the retained benchmarks.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a controlled analysis of continuing KL projections after reaching the final temperature, testing whether remaining error can be reduced without further annealing. The existing warm-start, stopping-parameter, preconditioner, entropy and smoothing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 5 adds 80% confidence intervals for CPU exact-solver timings; the corresponding v3 timing figure reported medians without these intervals. Existing 75% intervals in scaling and DOTmark plots remain. No increase in repeated runs or seeds is stated.

E6.justification: v4 adds CPU timings, Table 1 error/time/speedup entries and IPOT results. For example, Table 1 reports 11.85 seconds for MDOT-PNCG at 0.002% relative error versus 5.45 seconds for the exact solver on n = 4096 MNIST with L1 cost. Appendix G reports similar L1 behavior and up to 10-fold faster MDOT convergence for squared L2 under its new protocol. Retained benchmark results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDOT accuracy remark changes the sufficient condition from gamma_f = 5Hmin/(2epsilon) to gamma_f >= 5Hmin/(2epsilon). Appendix A.1 revises the duality derivation with explicit constants and multiplier shifts, and A.2 reorganizes the equivalence proof around Lemma 4.1. The principal MD/EOT equivalence and convergence-rate results remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introduction contributions retain the same scientific claims about MDOT, warm starting, PNCG and empirical efficiency. The conclusion preserves these claims; its added reference to subsequent work does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly acknowledges that the CPU exact solver offers a better high-precision trade-off at n = 4096 on the tested hardware, while discussing improved relative scaling for MDOT. Appendix G newly interprets the contrasting L1 and squared-L2 behavior through projection error versus entropic error.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly identifies the POT/Bonneel exact-cost implementation and Intel Xeon Silver 4110 CPU. Appendix G documents direct row/column reductions, operation counting and approximately 10^-30 numerical stabilization for its comparison implementation. Existing GPU, preprocessing and baseline implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds references on numerical continuation, mirror descent, exact OT/POT, barycenters and the authors' 2025 truncated-Newton work. It also expands the distinctions from iBPPA and IPOT, especially their projection stopping rules, while retaining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: Sections 2.2 and 4.1–4.2 and Appendix A receive extensive explanatory rewriting and internal reorganization. v4 adds a fuller mirror-descent introduction, a step-by-step MDOT guide, descriptive discussions of algorithm choices and an appendix roadmap. This substantially revises the exposition despite stable core methods.

P2.justification: v4 adds the MDOT schematic, IPOT plots and Table 1. It modifies the main timing figure with CPU timing lines, confidence bands, axis limits and legend placement, and adds scaling-reference lines to Figure 6. The journal template changes headers and layout, while most existing graphics are reused unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added IPOT and CPU exact-solver comparisons make the empirical assessment more informative and qualify the practical speed advantage, particularly at high precision. Clearer method exposition and newly disclosed implementation details also help readers assess and reproduce the work. These are useful, targeted improvements; the core method, claims and extensive existing benchmark evidence remain largely unchanged.
